A lathed part is milled on a Vertical Milling Machine for 13 minutes at a milling speed of 1000 rpm using an end mill with 4 flutes and a depth of cut of 3 mm to produce a milled part.

A wire EDM cutting operation is performed on a shaped part conveyed on a conveyor belt using a molybdenum wire with a peak current of 15A, pulse duration of 50ns, and a cutting speed of 0.1 mm/min, for 54 minutes, to produce a precision finished ground part that is transferred to a mobile robot.
On the Screw Machines, a lathed part is screwed using an M6 screw with a coarse thread for 38 minutes to produce a screwed component, with a production rate of 10 pieces per minute.

On a Vertical Lathe, a MetalBar is lathe turned for 69 minutes at a rotation speed of 600 rpm using a Carbide turning tool with a feed rate of 0.15 mm/rev to produce a LathedPart, which is then conveyed out on the ConveyorBelt.

A planing operation is performed on a Planer for 66 minutes to transform a milled part into a planed part, with a cut depth of 5 mm, a feed rate of 0.3 mm/rev, and a surface finish of Ra 1.6 µm, and both input and output components are conveyed on the ConveyorBelt.

A Horizontal Lathe Turning operation is performed on a Metal bar input component for 81 minutes using a High-speed steel tool at a rotation speed of 500 rpm and a feed rate of 0.1 mm/rev, resulting in a Lathed part output component on the ConveyorBelt.
